title: Problem Solving I
description: Discussion and solution of nonroutine mathematical problems related with different problem-solving techniques. Possible topics are: Pigeonhole principle, use of invariants and symmetries in problem solving, coloring arguments, parity, recursive arguments, extreme principle, inclusion-exclusion principle.

title: Problem Solving II
description: Discussion and solution of nonroutine problems in different areas of mathematics like Graph Theory, Number Theory, Combinatorics, Geometry, Game Theory, Topology, Algebra, and Analysis.

title: Topics in Modern Algebra
description: Topics may include groups; modules; vector spaces; algebras; metric structures on vector spaces; representation theory; multilinear algebra; graded structures; universal properties; a survey of important algebraic structures.

title: Advanced Linear Algebra I
description: An introduction to the theory of Linear Algebra with topics: Algebra of matrices, linear systems of equations, vector spaces, linear independence, basis and dimension, infinite-dimensional vectors spaces, linear transformations, matrix representation, isomorphisms, quotient spaces, dual spaces, and determinants.

title: Advanced Linear Algebra II
description: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and diagonalization. Canonical form under similarity: Jordan canonical form and rational canonical form, inner product and norm. Gram-Schmidt process, adjoint of a linear operator, normal and self-adjoint operators, unitary and orthogonal operators, spectral theorem.

title: Advanced Independent Research
description: Independent research on an original subject under faculty supervision carried out in a mathematics faculty reserach group. These advanced projects will attempt research of publishable quality; generally resulting in the preparation of a written report or manuscript for publication.

title: Introduction to Real Analysis
description: A rigorous introduction to the elements of analysis. Covers sequences, accumulation points, Bolzano-Weierstrass, Cauchy's criterion, the completeness property of the real number system, limits of functions, continuity, differentiability, compact sets, and the Heine-Borel theorem.

title: Special Topics in Mathematics
description: Lectures on a coherent body of mathematical topics which are not usually presented in standard mathematics courses.

title: Special Topics in Mathematics - Algebraic Geometry
description: An introduction to algebraic geometry, in which we study solutions of polynomial equations. We will focus on concrete examples from classical algebraic geometry, as well as the use of commutative algebra methods.

title: Introduction to Data Science and Machine Learning: Foundations and Applications
description: This course provides an accessible introduction to the field of data science and related techniques from machine learning. The course will develop both mathematical foundations and theory behind learning algorithms as well as discussing practical aspects for their use in applications.

title: Math Book Club
description: A collaborative seminar on mathematical topics not ordinarily covered in the standard curriculum. Students work as a cohort under faculty supervision to study a common textbook or collection of research papers. Participants give weekly presentations, lead peer discussions, and solve related problem sets. The course emphasizes independent learning within a shared seminar setting, with focus on mathematical reading, proof analysis, problem solving, and oral communication. Topic varies by term.

title: Special Topics in Mathematics: Combinatorics
description: Combinatorics has its historical roots in mathematical recreations and games. Combinatorics is concerned with arrangements of the objects in a set into patterns satisfying specified rules.

title: Special Topics in Mathematics: Category Theory
description: An introduction to category theory, suitable for sophomores in mathematics or computer science.

title: Theory of Distributions and their Applications
description: Distributions, also known generalized functions, are objects that generalize the classical notion of functions in mathematical analysis. Distributions make it possible to differentiate functions whose derivatives do not exist in the classical sense. Distributions are widely used in the theory of partial differential equations, in physics and engineering where many problems naturally lead to differential equations whose solutions or initial conditions are singular, such as the Dirac delta function.
